rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 384.9, best so far). The oval now finishes 19 of 20 runs at 1.97 s with rms 0.011 m, so the controller works on gentle curves. ki 0.5 helped there (oval mean 926 vs 808 in iteration 1). The s-bend (progress 0.43, about 1.0 line-loss event per run, steering oscillation 0.37) and slalom (progress 0.12, about 1.25 line-loss events per run) still leave the track by reaching the 0.06 m limit. Slalom progress is very low, so the robot fails at the first direction change. Earlier experiments that changed geometry or speed (sensor spacing, sensor size, base_speed) did not help, so I am leaving geometry alone. Change (controller only): kp 3.0 -> 3.5 for a firmer steer on sharp bends, and kd 0.8 -> 1.0 to damp the faster response and limit overshoot across the s-bend sign changes. ki stays at 0.5 because it helped the oval. Expected result: fewer line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom, with progress on those tracks rising by roughly 0.1 or more. The oval should still finish in under 2.1 s. Risk: steering_oscillation may rise above 0.4 on the s-bend, and if it does, kp should go back toward 3.0. Hypotheses to check: (a) slalom failures occur at the first sign change, where lateral error grows fastest; (b) higher kp with kd 1.0 reduces max_error without raising jitter; (c) if progress does not move, the limit is yaw response (wheel_track or mass), so the next test should change mass or wheel_track alone. Next measurements: progress, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation per track, plus completion_time on the oval.
